title: Your first custom design consultation
description: A little preparation helps turn your inspiration into a clear design conversation.
body: Start with the occasion
Think about where you will wear the outfit, how you want to feel and how much movement you need. Share the event date early so your designer can discuss a realistic schedule.
Collect a few references

Bring two or three images that show details you like. Explain whether it is the neckline, sleeve, colour or overall shape that appeals to you. References are a starting point for an individual design.
Discuss fit, fabric and budget
Mention fit preferences and a comfortable budget range. Ask about fabric suitability, measurements, fittings and what is included in the estimate.
Agree on the next step
Before leaving, confirm the design direction, quote, fitting arrangements and expected completion date. Keep a record of the agreed details.
author: Wear Mega-E Editorial

title: Choosing fabric for a special occasion
description: Look beyond colour: comfort, drape and structure matter too.
body: Consider the setting
An outdoor daytime event may call for different fabric from an indoor evening celebration. Consider temperature, movement and how long you will wear the outfit.
Understand the silhouette
Structured shapes need a fabric that can support them, while flowing looks benefit from a softer drape. Ask your designer to explain suitable options before buying material.
Check comfort and care
Look at how the fabric feels against your skin and whether it needs lining. Check care instructions and discuss any embellishments before committing.
author: Wear Mega-E Editorial

title: Keep your occasion outfits looking their best
description: Simple habits that protect delicate finishes between wears.
body: Follow the care label
Care requirements vary by fabric, lining and embellishment. Follow the garment label and seek professional advice if the instructions are unclear.
Store thoughtfully
Store clean garments away from damp and direct sunlight. Use suitable support for heavy designs and breathable covers where appropriate.
Handle delicate details gently
Avoid rubbing beading or lace against rough surfaces. Ask a specialist cleaner about a small stain before trying harsh treatments at home.
